package proto

import (
	"runtime"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"unsafe"
)

// Item 1: multiple direct calls (poly -> mul twice) and an indirect call
// through a unified function pointer (apply).
func TestDirectAndIndirect(t *testing.T) {
	// poly(x) = mul(x,x) + mul(x,3) = (x*x+7) + (x*3+7). poly reaches the
	// register-entry leaf mul through two direct calls. mul is internal-only
	// (SysV register arguments), so Go never calls it directly.
	if got := poly(0, 5); got != (25+7)+(15+7) {
		t.Fatalf("poly(5)=%d", got)
	}
}

// Item 1: the same signature behind a pointer, switched between a leaf's
// unified entry and a non-leaf. recPtr and polyPtr are unified entries.
func TestFunctionPointerSwitch(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		f    uintptr
		x    int64
		want int64
	}{
		{recUnifiedPC(), 10, 55 + 1},  // apply adds 1
		{polyUnifiedPC(), 5, 54 + 1},
	} {
		if got := apply(0, tc.f, tc.x); got != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("apply(%#x,%d)=%d want %d", tc.f, tc.x, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// Item 2: 16-byte JSValue by value, modify a copy, return a new value; the
// original is unchanged and the result is complete across a Go stack move.
func TestJSValueByValue(t *testing.T) {
	orig := JSValue{Tag: 1, Val: 10}
	got := bump(0, orig, 5)
	if orig.Tag != 1 || orig.Val != 10 {
		t.Fatalf("original mutated: %+v", orig)
	}
	if got.Tag != 1 || got.Val != 15 {
		t.Fatalf("bump result %+v", got)
	}
}

// Item 2: integer and floating-point arguments mixed.
func TestMixedIntFloat(t *testing.T) {
	if got := mix(0, 3, 1.5, 4); got != 8.5 {
		t.Fatalf("mix=%v", got)
	}
}

// Item 3 and 4: deep recursion forces repeated morestack with live unified
// frames; the correct sum proves the value held across each call (in the
// saved frame slot) is relocated on every stack move.
func TestRecursionMorestack(t *testing.T) {
	if got := rec(0, 100); got != 5050 {
		t.Fatalf("rec(100)=%d", got)
	}
	done := make(chan int64, 1)
	go func() { done <- rec(0, 300000) }()
	got := <-done
	want := int64(300000) * int64(300001) / 2
	if got != want {
		t.Fatalf("deep rec=%d want %d", got, want)
	}
}

// Item 3: GC runs while many goroutines execute unified frames.
func TestConcurrentGC(t *testing.T) {
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			for j := 0; j < 300; j++ {
				if rec(0, 4000) != 4000*4001/2 {
					panic("wrong sum under GC")
				}
			}
		}()
	}
	go func() {
		for i := 0; i < 500; i++ {
			runtime.GC()
		}
	}()
	wg.Wait()
}

// recUnifiedPC and polyUnifiedPC return the ABI0 code address of the unified
// entries, which the function table also holds (see table_amd64.s).
func recUnifiedPC() uintptr  { return unifiedTable[0] }
func polyUnifiedPC() uintptr { return unifiedTable[1] }

var _ = unsafe.Pointer(nil)
